lines.content: PolicyHarbor v1.6 (integration candidate) is a desktop client and follow-up manager for individual insurance agents who prefer typed commands. Keep client contact details and their next action together, then review what is overdue, due today or upcoming.
![PolicyHarbor showing pending follow-ups and a selected client profile](docs/images/Ui.png)
- Add, list, edit and delete clients, including distinct clients with the same name.
- Find clients by a name fragment, phone-number fragment or exact tag.
- Open a complete client profile with `view ID`, including contact details, sorted tags and the pending action. Permanent Client IDs stay unchanged across searches, edits and follow-up sorting.
- Record, replace or clear one dated follow-up per client.
- Keep an all-client pending summary visible beside searches and the selected profile, grouped with `OVERDUE`, `DUE TODAY` and `UPCOMING` badges.
- Save changes automatically to local JSON and reload them after restarting. Failed saves preserve the previous state; invalid saved files open a protected session.
- Submit commands with Enter or Run and correct rejected input using explicit, scrollable error feedback.
PolicyHarbor supports one pending action per client. Multiple actions, follow-up history and notifications are outside v1.6.

This project uses Gradle for **build automation and dependency management**. **We recommend reading [this Gradle tutorial from se-edu/guides](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/gradle.html).**
The following commands perform common Gradle tasks.
* **`clean`**: Deletes the files created during the previous build tasks (e.g. files in the `build` folder).
* **`shadowJar`**: Uses the Shadow plugin to create the fat JAR file `build/libs/PolicyHarbor.jar`.
**`runShadow`**: Builds the application as a fat JAR, then runs it.
* **`checkstyleMain`**: Runs the code style check for the main code base.
**`checkstyleTest`**: Runs the code style check for the test code base.
* `./gradlew clean test`: Cleans the project before running all tests
This project uses GitHub Actions for CI. The necessary workflow configuration files are in `.github/workflows`. No further setup is required.
As part of CI, Gradle generates JaCoCo coverage reports from the tests, and CI uploads the coverage data to Codecov. Codecov then provides information about test coverage.
Coverage is evidence for investigating untested behavior, not a fixed release percentage. Check the workflow result and report-upload logs rather than assuming a green badge proves correctness.
To enable Codecov for forks of this project, follow the steps given in [this se-edu guide](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/codecov.html).

In addition to Gradle checks, CI runs repository-wide checks. Unlike Gradle checks, which cover files used in the build, these checks cover every repository file and enforce rules that are hard to apply on development machines, such as line-ending requirements.

These checks are implemented as POSIX shell scripts, and thus can only be run on POSIX-compliant operating systems such as macOS and Linux. To run all checks locally on these operating systems, execute the following in the repository root directory:
Any warnings or errors will be printed out to the console.

* Checks are implemented as executable `check-*` scripts within the `.github` directory. The `run-checks.sh` script will automatically pick up and run files named as such. That is, you can add more such files if you need and the CI will do the rest.
* Check scripts should print out errors in the format `SEVERITY:FILENAME:LINE: MESSAGE`
* SEVERITY is either ERROR or WARN.
* FILENAME is the path to the file relative to the current directory.
* LINE is the line of the file where the error occurred and MESSAGE is the message explaining the error.
* Check scripts must exit with a non-zero exit code if any errors occur.

PolicyHarbor helps individual insurance agents manage contact records and one pending next action per client. This guide is for developers: start with component responsibilities, then follow the identity, command-publication and persistence invariants before changing the product. Exact command syntax is in the [User Guide](UserGuide.html).

**Version baseline:** this guide describes the v1.6 integration candidate at [`e185a9cc`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/tree/e185a9cc568a0cbde2225cc7e3ff3c200c39f568) and its merged bug fixes. Build the matching candidate using [DevOps](DevOps.html#building-a-candidate). `MainApp.VERSION` is `V1.6` and the window title is `PolicyHarbor v1.6`. v1.6 is not yet published; the [published v1.5 artifact record](Testing.html#published-v15-verification) remains historical evidence for that release, not certification of this candidate. Final publication must record the tested source SHA, uploaded JAR checksum and outstanding platform checks.

* [AddressBook Level 3 (AB3)](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3) is the starting codebase. PolicyHarbor retains `seedu.address`, the Java/JavaFX/FXML component-manager structure, common utilities and test/build conventions. Client identity, follow-ups, transactions, validation and dashboard behavior substantially adapt that foundation.

* The [AB3 Developer Guide](https://se-education.org/addressbook-level3/DeveloperGuide.html) and [User Guide](https://se-education.org/addressbook-level3/UserGuide.html) supplied documentation structure and retained architecture explanations. The architecture, component, class/parser and deletion diagrams under `docs/diagrams` derive from AB3 diagrams and have been adapted to PolicyHarbor's implemented relationships and execution flow. The project website retains the AB3 [Jekyll](https://jekyllrb.com/)/[Minima](https://github.com/jekyll/minima) foundation.

* The retained Metro-style button CSS in `DarkTheme.css` is adapted from [Pedro Duque Vieira's JMetro styles](https://pixelduke.wordpress.com/2012/10/23/jmetro-windows-8-controls-on-java/), as credited in that stylesheet.

* The homepage bundles a subset of [Newsreader, by the Newsreader Project Authors](https://github.com/productiontype/Newsreader), for headings in `docs/assets/landing/Newsreader.woff2`. Its SIL Open Font License 1.1 notice is retained in [`OFL.txt`](assets/landing/OFL.txt). The font is a reused asset, separate from the application implementation.

* Libraries: [JavaFX](https://openjfx.io/) supplies the GUI; [Jackson](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson) handles JSON storage, including its Java time module; [JUnit 5](https://docs.junit.org/5.14.4/overview.html) provides the automated test framework.

* Diagrams are authored with [PlantUML](https://plantuml.com/). [Gradle](https://gradle.org/) and the [Shadow plugin](https://gradleup.com/shadow/) build/package the application; [Checkstyle](https://checkstyle.org/) and [JaCoCo](https://www.jacoco.org/jacoco/) support code-style and coverage checks.

* The team used [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) and [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) to help write and review application code, tests and documentation, and to investigate bugs. Contributors remain responsible for reviewing and verifying the resulting work.

Refer to [_Setting up and getting started_](SettingUp.html) for the prescribed JDK/JavaFX and IDE setup. Keep synthetic test folders separate from real client data. Production entry points are `Main`/`MainApp`; test fixtures live in test sources and are not packaged commands.

:bulb: **Tip:** The `.puml` files used to create diagrams are in `docs/diagrams`. Refer to the [_PlantUML Tutorial_ at se-edu/guides](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/plantUml.html) to learn how to create and edit diagrams.

Class diagrams use solid associations, dashed dependencies, hollow triangles for generalization/realization and filled diamonds for composition. `<<interface>>` labels distinguish interfaces; italic class names identify abstract classes. Sequence diagrams use solid call arrows and dashed returns, with `alt` frames for alternative outcomes. On a narrow screen, scroll a figure horizontally or open its full-size image.

PolicyHarbor is an offline Java/JavaFX client and next-action manager. Components separate presentation, command orchestration, domain state and local persistence; the diagram shows selected dependencies, not class inheritance.

**`Main`** (consisting of classes [`Main`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/Main.java) and [`MainApp`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/MainApp.java)) is in charge of the app launch and shut down.

* At launch, `MainApp` acquires JAR-home ownership, loads/recovers preferences, constructs Storage, loads Model, then connects Logic and UI. A reported client-data loading error creates a protected model; see the [recovery limitation](#protected-startup-and-safe-replacement). It does not silently start a writable replacement dataset.

* At startup/focus and each minute, it refreshes the shared date used for action statuses. On shutdown it stops the timer, saves window preferences and releases instance ownership; UI closure disposes its observers and Help window.
The bulk of the app's work is done by the following four components:
* [**`Model`**](#model-component): Holds the data of the App in memory.
* [**`Storage`**](#storage-component): Reads data from, and writes data to, the hard disk.
[**`Commons`**](#common-classes) represents a collection of classes used by multiple other components.
**How the architecture components interact with each other**

Commands cross the UI → Logic → candidate Model → Storage boundary. The [transaction sequence](#save-before-publish-boundary) shows when changes become live; component/class diagrams below describe responsibilities without repeating that flow.
Each of the four main components (also shown in the diagram above),
* defines its _API_ in an `interface` with the same name as the Component.
* provides its functionality through a concrete `{Component Name}Manager` class that implements the corresponding API interface.

For example, the `Logic` component defines its API in `Logic.java` and implements it in `LogicManager.java`. Other components interact with a component through its interface rather than its concrete class, preventing them from coupling to that component's implementation, as illustrated in the following partial class diagram.
<figure class="uml-diagram" tabindex="0" aria-label="Component interfaces and manager implementations">
The sections below give more details of each component.
The **API** of this component is specified in [`Ui.java`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/Ui.java)
<figure class="uml-diagram" tabindex="0" aria-label="UI composition and shared UiPart base class">

The UI consists of a `MainWindow` and its parts, including `CommandBox`, `ResultDisplay`, `PersonListPanel`, `ClientProfilePanel`, `PendingFollowUpPanel` and `StatusBarFooter`. All of these, including `MainWindow`, inherit from the abstract `UiPart` class, which captures common behavior among classes that represent visible GUI parts.

The `UI` component uses the JavaFX UI framework. The layouts of these UI parts are defined in matching `.fxml` files in `src/main/resources/view`. For example, [`MainWindow.fxml`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/resources/view/MainWindow.fxml) specifies the layout of [`MainWindow`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/MainWindow.java).
* executes user commands using the `Logic` component.
* listens for changes to `Model` data so that the UI can be updated with the modified data.
* keeps a reference to the `Logic` component, because the `UI` relies on the `Logic` to execute commands.
* depends on some classes in the `Model` component because it displays `Person` objects from the model.
Here's a (partial) class diagram of the `Logic` component:
<figure class="uml-diagram" tabindex="0" aria-label="Logic, command and parser structure">

`LogicManager` dispatches commands, runs them on isolated model candidates, saves dirty client data and publishes only on success. Read-only commands publish view/selection/date without saving. See the [save-before-publish boundary](#save-before-publish-boundary) for the execution sequence and failure contract. `XYZCommand` is a representative concrete command, not a source class.
Parser delegation is shown separately to keep the command diagram readable:
<figure class="uml-diagram" tabindex="0" aria-label="Selected parsers and shared parsing utilities">

This partial diagram focuses on follow-up, view and search parsing. The shown parsers implement `Parser<T extends Command>` with their respective command result types. `ViewCommandParser` and `FollowUpCommandParser` share `ClientIdParserUtil.parseClientId()`. Add, edit and delete parsers and low-level tokenizer details are omitted to keep this view focused.

* When called upon to parse a user command, the `AddressBookParser` class creates an `XYZCommandParser` (`XYZ` is a placeholder for the specific command name, e.g., `AddCommandParser`). The parser uses the other classes shown above to parse the user command and create an `XYZCommand` object (e.g., `AddCommand`). The `AddressBookParser` returns that object as a `Command` object.

* All `XYZCommandParser` classes, such as `AddCommandParser` and `DeleteCommandParser`, implement the `Parser` interface so they can be treated similarly where appropriate, for example during testing.
<figure class="uml-diagram" tabindex="0" aria-label="Model ownership, permanent IDs and the optional follow-up">
* owns client records through `AddressBook`/`UniquePersonList`, with aggregate-owned permanent identity metadata independent of contact equality.
* derives one displayed list for full, search or pending mode and exposes a stable unmodifiable `ObservableList<Person>`.
* exposes read-only properties for the current date, pending-list mode and selected canonical client; these are session state and are not serialized.
* stores a `UserPrefs` object that represents the user’s preferences (currently, just the GUI settings). This is exposed to the outside as a `ReadOnlyUserPrefs` object.
* does not depend on any of the other three components (as the `Model` represents data entities of the domain, they should make sense on their own without depending on other components)
<figure class="uml-diagram" tabindex="0" aria-label="JSON storage and follow-up adapters">
* can save both client data and user preference data in JSON format, and read them back into corresponding objects.
* is implemented by `StorageManager`, which delegates the actual JSON file access to `JsonAddressBookStorage` and `JsonUserPrefsStorage` (one class per data file).
* depends on some classes in the `Model` component (because the `Storage` component's job is to save/retrieve objects that belong to the `Model`)

The [`seedu.address.commons`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/commons) package supplies shared exceptions, JSON/file/string utilities, GUI settings, logging and process locking. Domain rules stay in Model; common utilities do not own client state.

A table position changes after searching, deleting or sorting pending work. It cannot safely identify a client. [`ClientId`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/model/person/ClientId.java) is instead a permanent positive integer, independent of contact-value equality. Commands resolve it against the **complete** address book through `ClientIdResolver.requireClient`, including clients hidden by a filter.

[`AddressBook`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/model/AddressBook.java) owns both `UniquePersonList` and `ClientIdentityRegistry`. The registry associates canonical `Person` references with IDs and maintains a monotonic `nextClientId`. A canonical record is the actual immutable instance in the owning book; an equal-valued copy is not an identity key. Metadata is installed before list notifications, so observers can resolve newly published records.
| `addPerson` | Allocates the next ID; the command obtains it from the aggregate for feedback. |
| `setPerson(target, replacement)` | Transfers the canonical target's ID to the immutable replacement, retaining insertion position. Use this for contact/follow-up changes. |
| `removePerson` | Removes the association without lowering the allocation counter. |
| `setPersons` | Allocation-oriented bulk replacement: retained references keep IDs; reconstructed equal-valued records receive new ones. It is not an edit or snapshot API. |
| `resetData` / `restorePersons` | Copies an identity-bearing snapshot / restores a fully validated saved snapshot, including its counter. |

IDs range from 1 to 2147483647. The `long` counter can reach the exhausted sentinel 2147483648; allocation then raises `ClientIdExhaustedException`, which addition translates into a command error. Deleting records, including every record, does not release old IDs. A failed command candidate consumes no **live** ID. Normal save/restart retains gaps and the counter; externally removing all identity history is the [legacy compatibility limitation](#permanent-identity-in-json).

The central invariant is that a command must not publish client-data changes that could not be saved. [`LogicManager.execute`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/LogicManager.java) owns this boundary:

The candidate has its own aggregate/identity registry, observable list and session properties; immutable `Person` values may be shared. Parse or command failures publish nothing. A save failure becomes a `CommandException` with recovery guidance and discards the candidate, preserving live data, list mode/order, selected client and command date. The atomic storage writer preserves the destination on its reported write/move failure. Read-only commands publish view/date changes without saving client data.
<figure class="uml-diagram" tabindex="0" aria-label="Permanent-ID deletion and save-before-publish">

Deletion removes the identified client and their optional action. It retains the active list mode and clears selection only when necessary. The diagram assumes parsing and ID resolution succeed; it does not imply that deletion is committed before saving. An [alternative component-level sequence](images/ArchitectureSequenceDiagram.png) abstracts the same boundary.

**Trade-off:** candidate isolation avoids trying to roll back every observable UI effect after an I/O failure. It copies state and revalidates collections rather than optimizing for very large datasets. Performance targets are [requirements to measure](#non-functional-requirements), not a claim that copying is free.

Contact values (`Name`, `Phone`, `Email`, `Address`) and `Person` are immutable. Parsers and JSON adapters reconstruct the same domain values, so saved data cannot bypass validation. Unicode names, addresses and follow-up notes must contain valid, persistable text; unpaired UTF-16 surrogates are rejected even when produced by syntactically valid JSON escapes. Email validation and ordinary-space trimming use iterative scans, avoiding recursive-regex/large-input failure modes. The [UG's input reference](UserGuide.html) gives exact user-facing constraints.

[`Person.isDuplicateOf`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/model/person/Person.java) applies **normalized-name equality AND (same phone digits OR case-insensitive email equality)**. Name comparison uses NFC composition, collapsed ordinary-space runs and `equalsIgnoreCase`; stored spelling is retained. ASCII apostrophe (`'`) and smart apostrophe (`’`) are both accepted but remain distinct for duplicate comparison and name search. Names must begin with a letter or ASCII digit; the error message states this rule. Phone formatting is retained for display but ignored for this duplicate comparison. Address, tags and follow-up are excluded.

This relation is symmetric but **not transitive**: for one name, A `(111, one@example.com)` conflicts with B `(111, two@example.com)`, and B with C `(222, two@example.com)`, although A and C may coexist. `UniquePersonList` therefore checks every relevant pair, excluding only the replaced slot during an edit. It cannot safely use this relation as `equals`/`hashCode`. Full value equality still includes all stored fields and the action; `isSamePerson`'s legacy stored-name comparison is not permanent identity. Name-only rejection was also unsuitable because real clients can share names.

`Email` accepts internal ASCII apostrophes alongside its existing `+ _ . -` punctuation, while retaining its first/last alphanumeric and dot-adjacency restrictions; it does not implement every RFC email form. `Tag` accepts alphanumeric segments separated by single internal hyphens or underscores, lowercases with `Locale.ROOT`, and removes case variants through set equality. Leading, trailing or adjacent separators are rejected. `Tag.formatTags` supplies consistent sorted output to contact feedback, while the profile renders sorted chips. Duplicate checking covers the whole book, irrespective of the displayed filter.
### View parsing, client search and supported command routing

[`AddressBookParser`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/parser/AddressBookParser.java) first rejects raw control characters and line/paragraph separators, then normalizes only the command word with `Locale.ROOT` for case-insensitive dispatch. Only `add`, `delete`, `edit`, `view`, `find`, `list`, `followup` and `followups` are typed routes. Arguments retain their original case for command-specific parsing; field prefixes remain case-sensitive. Legacy command classes are not proof that `clear`, `help` or `exit` is accepted at the command box; Help/window closure are GUI actions.

Global character validation and command-word normalization precede the failed-load mutation gate. In a protected session, `add`, `delete`, `edit` and singular `followup` are rejected in every letter case before their command-specific parsers; queries remain available. Otherwise each parser checks its own shape/prefixes and values. `list`/`followups` reject arguments. Shared `ClientIdParserUtil` validates a bounded ASCII numeric ID (leading zeroes allowed); `ClientIdResolver` distinguishes a valid-but-absent ID during execution. A malformed command never changes the model merely because its prefix was recognized.

`FindCommandParser` constructs a predicate over all clients, replacing any earlier full/search/pending view. Bare keywords use whole-name-word **OR** exact-full-phone matching; explicit `n/`, `p/` or `t/` accepts exactly one field. `ClientSearchPredicate` implements normalized case-insensitive name substrings, phone-digit substrings ignoring display separators, and exact case-insensitive tags. Bare phone keywords retain leading zeroes and are not concatenated. Prefix mixing, quoted text and ordinary-space tokenization follow the shared grammar, rather than a general query language.

Invalid explicit phone/tag values produce field-specific constraints after query-shape checks; missing/repeated/mixed fields retain usage feedback. Valid tag separators follow `Tag.isValidTagName`, including single internal hyphens/underscores. `FindInvalidValueFeedbackTest` verifies rejected searches preserve state and saved bytes.

`FindCommand` accepts `Predicate<Person>`, keeping search policy outside the command. Search preserves insertion order, emits each client once and retains a selected profile only while its canonical record is visible. `ViewCommand` resolves IDs globally: viewing a hidden client first restores the full list; viewing an already visible client retains the current mode. Neither operation saves client data.

[`EditCommandParser`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/parser/EditCommandParser.java) requires an ID and at least one supplied field. Omitted fields remain unchanged; supplied tags replace the complete set, with a lone empty `t/` clearing it. Contact validation occurs during parsing, before execution resolves the ID. A multi-token preamble (for example `1 pp/92345678`) reports edit usage before ID parsing; a single invalid numeric token retains the existing ID error. Unrecognised prefix-like text such as `pp/` inside an address value remains literal; recognised prefixes such as `p/` following an ordinary space start a new field.

`EditCommand` creates an immutable replacement retaining the optional follow-up. `Model.setPerson` checks the full collection for duplicates, transfers the ID through the aggregate, and re-evaluates the active filter. Changing a search field can hide the edited client and clear selection; a failed save publishes none of these changes. This reuses the same replacement path as follow-up changes rather than assigning identity in individual commands.

`Person` contains **zero or one** immutable `FollowUp` with `dueDate : LocalDate` and `description : String`. Setting/replacing creates a new `Person` preserving contacts/tags/ID; clearing removes the optional value. There is no completion flag, notification scheduler or action history.

`FollowUpCommandParser` distinguishes `followup ID clear` from date/description input, accepting any letter case for the `clear` subcommand. The set command resolves the global ID before validating the raw date and description; date errors precede description errors. Past dates are allowed for overdue carry-over work. Calendar parsing is strict, with years 0001–9999. Notes retain Unicode spelling/internal spacing, trim outer ordinary spaces, and require 1–200 Unicode code points with visible content. The tokenizer recognizes space-prefixed `d/` and `m/` even inside a note; quotes do not escape them. These are deliberate grammar limits, documented in the UG.

`ModelManager.showPendingFollowUps()` includes every client with an action and stably sorts by due date. Ties retain full-list insertion order. `FollowUp.getStatus(today)` derives `OVERDUE`, `DUE_TODAY` or `UPCOMING` from the supplied date; the value does not read the device clock. Neither status nor selection is serialized.

`LogicManager` samples its clock once per command candidate and publishes that date only on success. Separately, `MainApp` refreshes the live date on startup, regained window focus and a one-minute timer. An idle window therefore updates across midnight; a failed command itself cannot advance the date, although an independent refresh can. ISO dates avoid dependence on the operating system's display format; the local clock/time zone still determine what counts as today.

For `followup 17 d/2099-12-15 m/Discuss renewal`, dispatch creates a `SetFollowUpCommand` with raw values. The command resolves ID 17 on its candidate, validates and replaces the client while transferring identity. Storage serializes the action's date/description with the contact and identity metadata. Successful publication updates the table, profile and global summary; all use the same published date for status. Failed execution or saving retains the previous action and views.

The profile is model-owned session state, independent of JavaFX row highlighting. [`Model.selectedPersonProperty()`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/model/Model.java) is a stable read-only property whose nullable value must be a canonical **visible** record. An equal-valued copy is insufficient. Selection changes do not mark client data dirty and are not persisted.
| Reorder pending rows / replace selected client's immutable value | Follows the same ID while visible. |
| Filter out or delete selected client | Clears; returning to `list` does not reopen it. |
| Clear selected client's action | Clears in pending mode; remains in full/search mode if visible. |
| Add another client | Preserves the current mode/eligible selection; does not select the addition. |

`forkForCommand(today)` copies data, view state and selection into isolated observables. `commitFrom(candidate)` retains the live observable objects and maps the candidate's selected **Client ID** back to the actual committed record. This matters when an identical follow-up replacement creates an equal-valued new object: an equal aggregate snapshot need not reset the live list, so publishing the candidate reference directly would leave selection outside it. Canonical reconciliation handles either retained or replaced live data.

Profile scroll continuity is presentation state. `ClientProfilePanel` caches the rendered ID before a replacement removes the old record from the registry. The same client keeps its reading position across edits/action replacement; a different client (even with the same name) starts at the top. Model membership remains authoritative.

`MainWindow.fillInnerParts()` composes the command/feedback bar, permanent-ID table, profile and grouped pending panel. It rejects repeated initialization. `Dashboard.css` owns host geometry/branding; component FXML/styles own their contents. Split panes allocate space without modifying model state.

`PersonListPanel` observes only `Logic.getFilteredPersonList()`, uses `Logic.getClientId` for labels and identity for the `VIEWING` marker, and enables due/status columns in pending mode. Rows clear recycled graphics. The table is unsortable by header; insufficient column width enables horizontal scrolling. Highlighting a row does not select a profile.

`PendingFollowUpProjection` instead consumes `Logic.getAllPersonList()`, the complete unmodifiable committed feed. It retains canonical references and stably sorts actions by due date, independent of search/pending filters. `PendingFollowUpPanel` groups this projection using the published date and observes selected-client changes for markers. There is no second client store or panel clock. `MainWindow` closes/disposes the projection and panel when hidden; cleanup is idempotent and guards queued callbacks.

Enter and Run use one `CommandBox` submission path; Run is not a default button that could also fire on Enter. Errors retain exact input and restore typing focus; success clears it. `MainWindow` explicitly chooses normal/error feedback, rather than classifying message wording. The selectable, scrollable `ResultDisplay` does not steal command focus. A separate persistent saved-data warning cannot be cleared by ordinary command feedback.

`ClientProfilePanel` observes selected-client/date properties and wraps contacts, sorted tag chips and action text in its own scroll pane. Phone, email, address and action labels expose context-menu and keyboard copy actions. Each activation reads the current selected model value, not cached label text; an absent value or disposed panel cannot copy stale content. `MainWindow` routes copy success/failure to `ResultDisplay` without submitting or clearing the command draft. The pending panel scrolls independently. Help is a separate F1/menu window with copy-link feedback and Escape closure; reopening restores an iconified Help window. The footer shows the real data path with a full-path tooltip. These controls do not change storage ownership.

[`JsonSerializableAddressBook`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/storage/JsonSerializableAddressBook.java) represents the aggregate snapshot; `JsonAdaptedPerson`, `JsonAdaptedTag` and `JsonAdaptedFollowUp` reconstruct domain values. All contacts and identities are validated before `AddressBook.restorePersons` publishes them. Missing optional tags/actions mean an empty set/no action; required values, duplicates and invalid identity associations fail the **whole** load, without accepting an earlier valid subset.
Only persistent contact/action/identity data is stored:

Serialization asks the aggregate for each canonical record's ID; it never infers IDs from display order. Adapters require integral JSON numbers in the ID/counter ranges. Restoration rejects repeated IDs and a counter not greater than every allocated ID. Empty books retain their counter, including exhaustion.

A file is legacy only if **every** client ID and the root counter are absent or null. Loading assigns insertion-order IDs 1..N with counter N+1, without rewriting; the first successful mutation writes the current schema. Once any identity value is non-null, incomplete/null metadata is invalid throughout. Rejecting partial metadata avoids silently assigning new identities to established records.

**Compatibility limitation:** externally removing/nullifying *all* identity history makes a migrated file indistinguishable from legacy input. Former gaps and the high-water counter cannot be recovered without a complete backup. Normal operations do not clear this metadata.

Client reads use strict UTF-8 (one initial BOM is accepted), reject a null root/trailing content, duplicate object properties, unknown client-schema fields and non-string saved text. Domain validation then rejects invalid values, including malformed UTF-16 from JSON escapes. A genuinely absent file means a new empty book. If absence cannot be established because access is denied, loading is attempted so an inaccessible existing file cannot be mistaken for a first launch.

When saved-client loading reports a `DataLoadingException`, `MainApp.initModelManager` creates an empty mutation-blocked model and the UI displays a persistent warning. Queries remain usable; command dispatch blocks mutations. Repairing permissions or JSON during that session does not unlock it: restart and successfully reload valid data before modifying clients.
An exceptionally deeply nested array supplied externally as `nextClientId` can fail before this protected session opens; see the [known technical limitation](#deeply-nested-externally-edited-json).

For saves, [`JsonAddressBookStorage`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/blob/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/storage/JsonAddressBookStorage.java) serializes a candidate, writes a sibling temporary file and atomically replaces the destination. Unsupported atomic replacement is a save failure, not a fallback to partial writing; failures attempt temporary-file cleanup. A symbolic-link destination is rejected before writing and again before replacement. These checks are best effort against external filesystem changes: a late path swap can replace the link itself, but the atomic move does not write through to its target. The instance lock coordinates PolicyHarbor processes, not external editors. Atomic replacement is not a backup/history service or a guarantee against hardware failure.

Preferences have a different recovery policy from client records. `JsonUserPrefsStorage` rejects explicitly null `guiSettings` and malformed/mapping failures; `MainApp.initPrefs` falls back to `UserPrefs` defaults and attempts to save the recovery. Missing settings retain defaults. Client loading proceeds independently, so invalid preferences alone do not block client mutations. Preference compatibility still ignores unknown properties and accepts the last repeated property; strict client-reader options are not imposed on the shared mapper.

`ApplicationHome.getHomeDirectory()` resolves the application's code-source URI to an absolute physical JAR directory, safely decoding spaces, Unicode and percent signs. JAR aliases share their target's home. Exploded IDE/Gradle classes use the working directory. The resolver has no logging or filesystem-write dependency and does not modify `user.dir`; missing or unsupported code sources fail explicitly. `MainApp` resolves preferences, client data and the instance lock under this home. There is no automatic migration from an earlier working-folder dataset; the UG gives backup/manual relocation steps.

Before preferences/client loading, `MainApp.init()` acquires an OS file lock through `AppInstanceLock` on `.policyharbor.lock` in the application home. A competing launch or lock I/O failure leaves services uninitialized; startup explains the error and exits without preference writes. Initialization failure, normal shutdown or process termination releases ownership.

The marker is retained: deleting it while an owner holds the original file could let another process lock a replacement. An in-process registry rejects duplicate acquisitions before opening another descriptor, whose closure can release existing OS locks on some systems. Separate physical JAR homes remain independent. Launching the same JAR from different working directories shares one lock. This prevents simultaneous PolicyHarbor writers to one application home, without introducing a server or remote authentication.

`JsonUtil.readJsonFile` logs only path and failure category, excluding Jackson messages/throwables that can contain raw client data. It retains the cause in `DataLoadingException` for callers; that does not make the cause safe to print in ordinary diagnostics. Command submission logs outcome/category without raw input. These safeguards limit accidental disclosure in local diagnostic files; they do not encrypt the user's local client data.

`Main` and `MainApp` obtain loggers during static initialization, before `MainApp.init()`. `LogsCenter` therefore resolves `policyharbor.log` through `ApplicationHome` before constructing its `FileHandler`, after installing console logging. Literal `%` characters are doubled to `%%` for FileHandler pattern syntax, preserving the physical path without expanding `%h`, `%t`, `%g` or `%u`. Append mode, the 5 MiB rotation threshold and five-file retention remain unchanged. A file-handler `IOException` produces a generic warning and leaves console logging available; other initialization failures propagate. This fallback does not make client/preference writes succeed in an unwritable folder.

**System:** PolicyHarbor. **Actor:** individual insurance agent. Unless an extension states otherwise, the app has loaded valid data. Commands are single submissions; the system does not prompt for separate fields or confirmation. These use cases cover distinct interaction patterns; routine add/delete/list syntax is in the UG and manual appendix.
#### UC01 — Retrieve a client hidden by the current view
**Preconditions:** the client exists with a known permanent ID; the table is filtered or in pending mode and hides that client.
1. Agent requests the client's profile using their permanent ID.
2. System resolves the ID against the complete client collection, restores the full list and opens the correct profile.
Use case ends. Saved data remains unchanged.
* 1a. The request has invalid syntax or an invalid ID value.
* 1a1. System explains the format/ID constraint and retains the current view and profile.
* 2a. No client has that valid ID.
* 2a1. System reports the missing ID and retains the current view and profile.
#### UC02 — Edit a client while retaining their identity
**Preconditions:** the client exists; client mutations are not blocked by startup recovery. The agent has the permanent ID and at least one replacement field.
1. Agent submits contact changes for that ID.
2. System validates the supplied fields, resolves the client and checks other records for duplicates.
3. System saves the replacement with the same ID and pending action, then publishes it and success feedback.

Use case ends. The active filter is retained. An existing profile remains open while its client is visible; if that client was edited, it shows the replacement. Editing does not open an unselected client's profile.
* 1a1. System explains that saved data must be repaired/restored and reloaded; no changes are accepted.
* 2a. Fields/ID are invalid, the ID is absent or the replacement duplicates another client.
* 2a1. System explains the relevant error and retains data, filter and selection.
* 3a1. System gives recovery guidance and keeps the previous live record, ID, action, view and saved file.
* 3a2. Agent addresses the filesystem problem and retries.
#### UC03 — Record, replace or clear a next action
**Preconditions:** the client exists with a known ID; mutations are allowed. A replacement/clear request concerns the client's single pending action.
1. Agent submits a date and action description for that ID.
2. System resolves the client and validates the date and description.
3. System saves the new action, replacing any previous one, then publishes the updated client and pending views.
Use case ends. The ID/contacts are retained; pending order and status reflect the new date, and any visible selected profile follows the same client.
* 1a. Agent instead requests that the action be cleared.
* 1a1. System resolves the client and confirms an action exists.
* 1a2. System saves/publishes its removal. The client leaves the pending list; that client's open profile clears there but remains in full/search mode while visible.
* 1a1a1. System explains this and makes no changes.
* 2a. Input/ID is invalid or the ID is absent.
* 2a1. System explains the error; the previous action, data and view remain unchanged.
* 3a1. System gives recovery guidance and preserves the previous action, data, view and saved file; no tentative reorder is published.
* 1a2a1. System gives recovery guidance and preserves the previous action, data, view and saved file; no tentative removal is published.

* **Client record:** contact details/tags and, optionally, one pending action for a client or prospect.
* **Client ID:** permanent positive integer allocated by the address book; unrelated to row position and not reused after normal deletion.
* **Canonical record:** the actual immutable `Person` instance registered in its owning address book, rather than an equal-valued copy.
* **Follow-up:** next action with a due date and description.
* **Pending:** recorded and not cleared, including actions whose dates have passed.
* **Overdue / due today / upcoming:** due date is before / equal to / after the published local date.
* **Protected startup:** empty query-capable session that blocks client mutations when loading reports a data error; see the [known recovery limitation](#protected-startup-and-safe-replacement).

* The project uses the `java.util.logging` package for logging.
* A class obtains a `Logger` with `LogsCenter.getLogger(Class)`, which logs messages at the configured level.

* Log messages are written to the console and rotating `policyharbor.log` files beside the physical JAR, regardless of the terminal working directory. Exploded IDE/Gradle classes use their working directory.

* If a diagnostic file cannot be opened, `LogsCenter` reports a generic warning through its initialized base logger and continues with console logging. It catches only `IOException` from file-handler setup; it does not suppress other initialization failures or change client-data/preference write handling.
* The output logging level can be controlled by changing the `LOG_LEVEL` constant in the `LogsCenter` class.

Drag the main divider to change the table/sidebar widths and the sidebar divider to change the profile/summary heights. Long values wrap; scroll each right-hand panel independently. A Client ID identifies one client permanently. It does not change when you search, reorder follow-ups or edit contact details. Read it from the table, profile, summary card or add feedback. Gaps after deletion are normal; IDs are not reused during normal operation.

**An ID is not a row position.** If a search shows only Client ID 8, `delete 1` targets Client ID 1, even if that client is hidden. Always check the ID and, before a change, use `view ID` to confirm the intended client.

`view`, `edit`, `delete` and `followup` resolve IDs against **all saved clients**, including clients hidden by a search or the pending list. IDs use digits `0`–`9` and range from `1` to `2147483647`. Leading zeroes are allowed: `view 001` and `view 1` select the same client. See [backup precautions](#existing-files-client-ids-and-backups) before moving or modifying ID history.
### Keeping the same client profile open

A viewed client is marked `VIEWING` in the table and, when they have an action, the summary. The profile shows their ID, contact details, lowercase tag chips and pending action. With no tags it shows `No tags`; without an action, `Follow-up: None`.

To copy a client's phone, email, address or follow-up action, **right-click its value** and choose **Copy phone**, **Copy email**, **Copy address** or **Copy follow-up action**. You can also **Tab** to focus the value and press **Enter**, **Space** or the copy shortcut (**Ctrl+C** on Windows/Linux, **Command+C** on macOS).

The complete current value is copied, including spaces and Unicode text; copying an action copies its description, without the due date. Feedback confirms success, such as `Copied phone.`, or reports `Could not copy phone.` if the clipboard is unavailable. Your command draft stays unchanged. A missing client or cleared action cannot be copied; an unavailable action reports `No follow-up action to copy.`
| What you do | What happens to the open profile |
| `list`, add another client or change another client's action | The same client stays open. |
| Search, show pending actions or edit details used by a search | The client stays open only if they remain in the displayed table; otherwise the profile closes. |
| Replace the viewed client's action | Their profile updates and follows the same ID, even if the row moves. |
| Clear their action | The profile stays open in full/search mode; it closes in pending mode because the client leaves that table. |
| Delete the viewed client | The profile closes without selecting someone else. |

When a profile closes, later returning to the full list does not reopen it; use `view ID` again. Restarting also clears profile selection. Opening a different client starts at the top; updating the same client's details/action or refreshing the date keeps the reading position as far as the remaining content allows. A failed command or save preserves the previous profile.

Successful commands clear the command field. Rejected commands keep the input for correction, mark the field and show **Error** above the message. For example, after `view 0`, correct the retained line to `view 1` for Rachel. Editing removes the field's error style; feedback stays until the next command. Long feedback wraps, scrolls and can be selected/copied.

Paste one command line at a time. A paste containing a tab, control character or line separator is rejected as a whole: the previous draft and selection remain, and no command runs. Remove those characters before pasting again. If you press Enter after a rejected paste, the unchanged previous draft is what runs.
| [Add a client](#adding-a-client-add) | `add n/NAME p/PHONE_NUMBER e/EMAIL a/ADDRESS [t/TAG]...` |
| [Find clients](#finding-clients-find) | `find KEYWORD [MORE_KEYWORDS]...` or `find n/NAME_PART`, `find p/PHONE_PART`, `find t/TAG` |
| [Record or replace an action](#recording-or-replacing-a-follow-up-followup) | `followup ID d/DATE m/DESCRIPTION` |
- Replace `UPPER_CASE` words with your values. Do not type the square brackets: they mark optional fields. `...` means tags or bare search keywords may be repeated as shown.

- Command words and the `clear` subcommand are case-insensitive: `LIST`, `Find Rachel` and `followup 1 CLEAR` work like their lowercase equivalents. Use ordinary spaces to separate words; extra ordinary spaces around a command are accepted. Tabs, control characters and line separators are rejected.

- Named fields such as `n/` and `p/` may be supplied in any order. Prefixes remain lowercase and case-sensitive. Put a space before each prefix. Required fields cannot be omitted or empty; `edit ID t/` is the special case for clearing tags.

- Do not repeat single-valued fields such as `n/` or `d/`; `t/` may repeat. Known prefixes within values can be interpreted as fields, and quotes do not escape them. See the [prefix reference](#prefixes-and-literal-text).
- `list` and `followups` take **no arguments**. For example, `list 123` is rejected with usage feedback.

Standalone `clear`, `help` and `exit` are unsupported and report `Unknown command.`. Clear an action with `followup ID clear`, open Help through the menu/F1 and close the app through the window or File → Exit.

The reference examples below use Rachel with Client ID 1. They illustrate each command independently; substitute your client's actual ID. In particular, try deletion only with disposable data, as it removes the client used in the other examples.

add n/Rachel Lim p/91234567 e/rachel@example.com a/Blk 123 t/health

A duplicate is rejected when the **name matches and either the phone or email matches** an existing client. Names ignore case, equivalent accented spellings and repeated ordinary spaces; phone comparison ignores allowed formatting, and emails ignore case. Straight `'` and curly `’` apostrophes remain distinct in names: `Sean O'Brien` and `Sean O’Brien` do not count as the same name. Address, tags and follow-up are not part of the check. Two clients may have the same name if both phone and email differ; different names may share contact details. Hidden clients are also checked.
For example, after adding Rachel, `add n/RACHEL  LIM p/91234567 e/other@example.com a/Blk 456` reports `This client already exists in PolicyHarbor.`

Adding preserves the current table mode and open profile. In a search, the new client appears only if they match; in pending mode, they stay hidden until they have an action. To see all clients, use `list`.
Return to all clients in the order they were added.
**Result:** `Listed all clients.` The current profile stays open. This leaves search/pending mode without changing data or IDs. Extra arguments are rejected; use `find` to search.
Search all clients, including those hidden by the current view. Results appear once per client in the order clients were added.

| Whole name words or a full phone number | `find KEYWORD [MORE_KEYWORDS]...` | `find Rachel Lim` matches either complete name word, ignoring case. `find 92345678` matches those complete phone digits. |
| Part of a name | `find n/NAME_PART` | `find n/rac` matches Rachel. |
| Part of a phone number | `find p/PHONE_PART` | `find p/9234` matches Rachel's edited phone from the quick start. |
| Exact tag | `find t/TAG` | `find t/HEALTH` matches the whole tag `health`, ignoring case. |

**Result:** feedback gives the count, such as `1 client(s) listed!`. Search leaves pending mode. The profile remains open only if the viewed client is among the results; the global summary still shows every pending action.

Bare search uses **either** keyword, not all keywords together: `find Rachel 92345678` returns clients matching either. Partial words do not match in bare mode: `find Rach` does not find Rachel; `find n/Rach` does. Bare phone search requires all stored digits, including any country code and leading zeroes. Separate tokens are not joined into one phone number.

Explicit name search ignores case, equivalent accented spellings and repeated ordinary spaces. Straight `'` and curly `’` apostrophes are distinct in both name search modes: use the spelling stored in the name, or search for a part without the apostrophe. Phone search ignores stored `+`, spaces and hyphens, and accepts a fragment of one or more digits with valid phone formatting. `find t/new` does not match `renewal`. Email and address are not searched; quotes and punctuation are literal text.

Invalid phone searches such as `find p/9123  4567` report phone-query constraints: at least one digit, an optional leading `+`, and single spaces or hyphens between digit groups. Invalid tags such as `find t/health!` report tag constraints; `find t/life-insurance` is valid. These errors leave the table, profile and saved records unchanged.

Use **one** explicit field, without bare text before it. `find n/Rachel p/9234`, repeated fields, empty values or `find` alone produce usage feedback. The prefixes `n/`, `p/` and `t/` remain reserved inside explicit queries.
Open the client's complete profile so you can check their details before acting.

**Result:** for Rachel, `Showing client ID 1: Rachel Lim`; her profile opens and her row is marked `VIEWING`. If she was hidden, the app first returns to the full list. If she was visible, the current mode and order stay unchanged. Viewing does not change saved data.

Supply one existing [Client ID](#permanent-client-ids). An unknown ID reports, for example, `No client with ID 1.`; this is different from an invalid number such as `0`. A failed view preserves the previous profile and table.
Update contact details while retaining the client's **ID and pending follow-up**. The target can be hidden by the current view.

**Result:** Rachel's phone changes; feedback starts `Client ID 1 updated: Rachel Lim`. Omitted fields keep their values. At least one field must be supplied; `edit 1` alone reports `At least one field to edit must be provided.`

A mistyped prefix after an ID, such as `edit 1 pp/92345678` or `edit 1 phone/92345678`, produces edit usage feedback. Correct it to `edit 1 p/92345678` and retry. An invalid numeric ID such as `0` still reports the ID constraint. Text already inside a recognised value, such as `edit 1 a/Home pp/unit`, remains literal address text.

**Supplying tags replaces the entire tag set.** For example, `edit 1 a/Blk 456 t/renewal t/priority` changes the address and replaces all previous tags with `priority` and `renewal`. Use a lone empty `t/`, as in `edit 1 t/`, to remove all tags.

The [contact field rules](#contact-field-reference) and duplicate check used for adding also apply to editing. An edit that duplicates another client reports `This person already exists in PolicyHarbor.` The current table mode remains, but search results are checked again: changing a matching field can hide that client and close their profile. Rejected edits keep the previous data.
Remove an incorrect or unwanted client record and their pending follow-up.

**Result:** Rachel and her action disappear; feedback starts `Deleted client ID 1: Rachel Lim`. If she was viewed, her profile closes. The current table mode remains, and other clients keep their IDs.

**Deletion is saved immediately, with no confirmation or undo.** It also removes the client's current action. Verify the ID with `view ID` first and keep a [backup](#existing-files-client-ids-and-backups) if you may need the record again. Deleting a hidden client works too; the first displayed row is not necessarily Client ID 1.
Each client can have **one pending action**. An overdue action stays pending until you clear it. The examples use Rachel's actual ID, shown as 1 here, and assume she has not been deleted.
Record a dated next action, or replace the client's current one.

**Result:** for a client without an action, feedback is `Follow-up for client ID 1: Rachel Lim recorded for 2099-12-15.` For a client with an action, it is `Follow-up for client ID 1: Rachel Lim updated to 2099-12-15.` The profile/summary refresh; in pending mode, a changed date can move the row while retaining the selected client.
**Replacing overwrites the previous date and description.** There is no history or undo; copy any details you need before replacing an action.
Use an actual calendar date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format, with a year from `0001` to `9999`. Past, current and future dates are accepted, so you can record overdue work using its original due date.

Descriptions allow multilingual text and emoji and must contain visible text or a symbol. The limit is **1–200 Unicode code points**, after trimming outer ordinary spaces; most letters count once, but joined emoji and accented combinations can count as several. Internal spacing is retained. Controls, line breaks, invalid characters and notes made only of invisible characters/combining marks are rejected.

The prefixes `d/` and `m/` preceded by an ordinary space are reserved even inside descriptions and quotes. For example, `m/Confirm d/m/y format` is rejected as a repeated date field. Write `m/Confirm day/month/year format` instead; `m/Check ref:d/m/y` is also valid because the internal `d/` has no preceding space.
Remove the current action after completing it, while keeping the client.

**Result:** `Follow-up for client ID 1: Rachel Lim cleared.` Their summary card disappears. In pending mode, the client also leaves the table and their profile closes; in full/search mode, the client remains and their open profile shows no action.
Clearing is saved immediately and has no undo/history. If there is no action, the result is `This client has no pending follow-up.`; no client is deleted.
Review clients with actions still to do, in **earliest due-date order**. Equal dates keep the order the clients were added.
**Result:** `Pending follow-ups`, or `There are no pending follow-ups.` if none remain. Extra arguments are rejected. `list` returns to all clients; `find` searches the full dataset.
The global summary groups the same actions by status, retaining due-date order within each group:

Statuses use the computer's current local date and refresh at startup, when the main window regains focus and once a minute while running. No command is needed to refresh them. Dates remain in `YYYY-MM-DD` format regardless of your computer's date display format.

Successful `add`, `edit`, `delete` and singular `followup` changes are saved automatically before appearing in the workspace. There is no save command. `list`, `find`, `view` and `followups` do not rewrite client data.

In v1.6, `data/addressbook.json` is inside the folder containing the **executed JAR**, regardless of the terminal's working directory. The footer shows the absolute data-file path. `preferences.json`, `.policyharbor.lock` and rotating `policyharbor.log.*` diagnostics use that same JAR folder. A symbolic link to the JAR uses the physical target JAR's folder; separate copies in different folders have independent datasets. IDE/Gradle runs use their working directory instead.

For example, launching `java -jar "/path/to/clients/PolicyHarbor.jar"` from another folder still loads `/path/to/clients/data/addressbook.json`. Diagnostic logs are local files; back up and share them with care.
After restarting the same JAR, contacts, IDs and pending actions return. The app starts with the full client list and no open profile; search/pending mode and profile selection are not restored.
A failed save keeps the previous client data, table and profile, and retains the rejected command for correction/retry. For a normal write failure, feedback says:
Could not save to /path/to/JAR-folder/data/addressbook.json. No changes were kept. Check that the data folder is writable and has free space, then try again.

The path in the message is your actual data-file location; the path above is illustrative. Restore access to the data folder and free disk space as needed, then submit the retained command again. Do not assume a failed add received an ID or that an unsuccessful edit/delete/action change was saved. The [troubleshooting table](#troubleshooting) covers protected data and symbolic-link errors separately.

v1.5 used the terminal's working folder; v1.6 does **not** automatically import files from that old location. Before upgrading, close every instance and back up the old `data/addressbook.json` and `preferences.json`. Put the new JAR in that old folder to keep using its files, or copy the complete client file into the new JAR folder's `data` subfolder. Copy preferences only if you want to retain window settings. Back up any destination files first; do not overwrite or combine two datasets without choosing which complete copy to keep. Do not copy or delete an active lock file. Restart and check the footer path and several client IDs before making changes.
### Existing files, Client IDs and backups

**Back up the complete `data/addressbook.json` while the app is closed.** There is no automatic backup or undo. Restore backups while closed, then restart; restoring an older copy replaces newer saved work with that copy's contents.

To transfer data, close the app on both computers. Put the matching JAR in a writable folder on the destination, create its `data` subfolder and copy the complete client file there, backing up any existing destination file first. Launch the new JAR copy with Java 25.

IDs and allocation history survive normal restarts and deletion, including deleting every client. Copying only contact entries, discarding identity fields or restoring an older backup can lose that history. Never reset IDs or lower their allocation counter as a repair. See [advanced file compatibility](#advanced-data-file-reference) if you maintain saved files directly.

The **Help → Help** menu or **F1** opens a window with the online User Guide link. Use **Copy link** or select/copy the link field, then open it in your browser. `Esc` closes Help. Opening Help again restores a minimised Help window and brings it forward. Core client/action commands work offline; opening the online guide needs Internet access.

| The JAR does not start | Launch from a terminal with `java -version` and `java -jar "PolicyHarbor.jar"`. Confirm Java 25 and the actual JAR filename. Double-clicking may use another Java installation. |

| Startup fails on macOS | Follow the [prescribed JavaFX/JDK setup](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/javaInstallationMac.html). Check `java -version` and `which java` in the same terminal before launching. |

| Linux shows `Gdk-CRITICAL` under Wayland | Try `GDK_BACKEND=x11 java -jar "PolicyHarbor.jar"`, as advised in the [course JAR testing instructions](https://nus-cs2103-ay2627-s1.github.io/website/schedule/week11/project.html). |

| A command is rejected | Read the complete feedback, correct the retained line and retry. Use lowercase field prefixes and one line with ordinary spaces. Command words accept any letter case. See the [command overview](#command-overview) and [field reference](#contact-field-reference). |
| A new or edited client seems missing | Run `list`: an active search can hide non-matching clients, and pending mode hides clients without actions. IDs have not changed. |
| `No client with ID ...` | Check the table/profile ID, not the row position. The client may have been deleted or belong to another data folder. |

| Changes cannot be saved | Check write access, free space and whether a regular file is blocking the `data` folder. Restore access, then retry. Do not run as administrator just to bypass permissions. |

| Saved-data warning; changes are blocked | Follow [protected-data recovery](#saved-data-warning-and-recovery). Restoring folder access or editing a file does not unlock the running session; restart to reload. |

| Another instance is running | Use or close the existing window for that JAR home. Launching the same JAR from another terminal folder still shares its lock; JAR copies in separate folders have independent data. |

| The folder cannot be locked | Use a writable folder. `.policyharbor.lock` must be a regular file; it normally remains after closing. Its presence alone does not mean the app is running. Do not delete/replace it while an instance runs; closing/terminating that instance releases the operating-system lock. |

| The data file is a symbolic link | Saving through it is refused. Close the app, back up the link's target, then replace the link with a regular data file and restart. Do not change data paths externally while the app is open. |

| Window settings are invalid or a saved screen was disconnected | Invalid `preferences.json` falls back to default settings and may be replaced; a preference error alone does not block client changes. A missing saved screen causes the window to fit on the primary screen; deleting client data is unnecessary. |

| The workspace feels cramped | Maximise the main window and adjust its dividers. Scroll the table horizontally and the profile/summary vertically. Secondary windows can behave differently across platforms; keep Help in an ordinary window if fullscreen causes trouble. |

| Diagnostic logging is unavailable | The launch terminal reports `Unable to create diagnostic log file; continuing with console logging.` The app keeps running. Check write access to the JAR folder and that `policyharbor.log.0` there is not a directory, then restart to restore file logging. |

When loading reports a saved-data error, the app shows an empty table and a persistent warning. **This does not mean your saved clients were deleted.** `add`, `edit`, `delete` and `followup` are blocked to protect the file; query commands remain available. An ordinary command result does not dismiss the warning.

1. Before closing, note the **data-file path at the bottom of the main window**; hover over a shortened path to read it in full. Separate JAR copies can use different client files. Close PolicyHarbor and back up that exact file if you can access it. Do not delete the only copy of client data to make the warning disappear.
2. If the folder was inaccessible, restore access. Otherwise restore a complete known-good backup, or have the file repaired using the [advanced reference](#advanced-data-file-reference).

3. Restart the same JAR copy to reload the file. If the client file is absent and that absence can be confirmed, the app starts a new, writable dataset. The app does not partly load a file containing invalid records.

4. Run `list`, then `view ID` using an ID from the restored table, and check the expected contact details and follow-up. If expected clients are still missing, check the footer path and backup you restored before adding replacement records; an empty list alone does not confirm successful recovery.

**Known startup limitation:** an externally edited client file with extremely deeply nested data can stop the app before the dashboard or saved-data warning appears. Normal app commands cannot create this problem. Close the app and preserve the original file, then restore a complete known-good backup to the JAR's `data/addressbook.json` or have the file safely repaired before restarting. The protected empty workspace is not available in this case; do not delete your only copy to get past startup.

- **Complete contact details are required.** Adding a prospect requires a name, phone, valid email and address. Unknown email/address values cannot be omitted or left empty, so a prospect with incomplete details cannot yet be recorded. See [adding a client](#adding-a-client-add).

- **Shared contacts can trigger duplicate rejection.** Distinct people with matching normalised names and either a matching phone or email cannot both be stored, even if they share that contact legitimately. There is no override; see the [duplicate rules](#adding-a-client-add).

- **Tag changes replace the whole set.** `edit ID t/TAG` does not append a tag: supply every tag you want to retain. `edit ID t/` clears all tags. See [editing details](#editing-a-clients-details-edit) for the full syntax.

- **Rescheduling requires the description again.** Use `followup ID d/DATE m/DESCRIPTION`; a date-only change is unsupported. You can copy the existing description from the profile before [replacing the action](#recording-or-replacing-a-follow-up-followup). Each client has one current action, with no follow-up history, reminders or notifications.

- **Searches do not combine.** Only one explicit field is accepted: `find n/Lim t/health` is unsupported. Each new search replaces the previous filter rather than narrowing its results. Email/address searches are unsupported; see [search options](#finding-clients-find).

- **Profiles open through `view ID`.** Clicking or highlighting a table row does not open its profile. Use the permanent Client ID shown in the table, not its row position; see [selecting a client](#selecting-a-client-view).

- **Successful commands cannot be recalled with Up/Down.** There is no command history. Failed input stays available for correction; see the [keyboard workflow](#keyboard-workflow-and-error-correction) for ways to reuse command text.

- **Saved changes have no undo.** Successful edits, deletions and follow-up changes save immediately. Check the intended client with `view ID` before changing their details. Backups are manual; restoring one replaces later changes. See [backup precautions](#existing-files-client-ids-and-backups).

- **Mixed Chinese/Tamil action text can display incorrectly** on some macOS/JavaFX setups, although the stored text remains intact. This affects readability of some mixed-language descriptions; a portable workaround has not been verified.

- **Exceptionally nested, externally edited files can prevent startup**, before the dashboard or protected-data warning opens. Follow [saved-data recovery](#saved-data-warning-and-recovery), preserving the original file before restoring a complete known-good backup or arranging a safe repair.
PolicyHarbor stores contacts and next actions. It does not manage insurance policy, premium or claim records; send messages; import/export CSV; or synchronise with cloud services.

These rules apply to both adding and editing. Ordinary spaces at the outside of field values are removed; internal spacing, spelling and case are retained except that tags become lowercase. There are no additional contact-length limits.

| Name | Starts with a letter from any language or a digit `0`–`9`. Supports Unicode letters with combining accents, ordinary spaces and `/ - ' ’ @ .`. Both the straight apostrophe `'` and curly right apostrophe `’` (U+2019) are accepted and retained as typed. A name must contain visible content; invisible Hangul fillers alone are rejected. Examples: `Ravi s/o Kumar`, `Sean O'Brien`, `Sean O’Brien`, `Dr. Lim`. |

| Phone | At least three digits `0`–`9`, optionally beginning with `+`, with single spaces or hyphens between digit groups. For example, `+65 9123 4567`. Display formatting and leading zeroes are retained. |

| Email | One `@`, with ASCII letters/digits and supported punctuation; no spaces. Before `@`, the first/last characters must be letters/digits; `+`, `_`, `-`, straight apostrophes `'` and periods may occur inside. Each period must have a letter/digit immediately on both sides. For example, `o'connor@example.com` is accepted; a curly apostrophe `’` is not. Domain labels start/end with letters/digits and may contain hyphens; the final label needs two adjacent letters/digits. Stored case is retained. |

| Address | Non-empty, single-line text with visible content, including punctuation, non-English text and emoji. Text made only of spaces/invisible formatting, controls or invalid character sequences is rejected. |

| Tag | One or more English letters or digits, optionally separated by single internal hyphens `-` or underscores `_`. For example, `life-insurance` and `high_priority` are valid; leading/trailing separators, adjacent separators such as `life--insurance`, spaces and other punctuation are rejected. Tags become lowercase; repeated case variants become one tag. |

Tags have no count limit. They display in lowercase alphabetical order; command feedback uses bracketed tags separated by spaces. Missing required fields, repeated single-valued prefixes and invalid values produce feedback to guide correction. When several values are invalid, correct the reported error and resubmit rather than assuming every problem was listed.

Recognised field prefixes are lowercase and case-sensitive and must follow an ordinary space. For add/edit, these are `n/`, `p/`, `e/`, `a/` and `t/`; for recording an action, `d/` and `m/`. For example, `EDIT 1 n/Rachel Lim` uses a recognised name prefix, but `EDIT 1 N/Rachel Lim` does not. Quotes are literal characters, not a way to escape a recognised prefix. Avoid putting a space followed by a command's recognised prefix inside a value.

Unrecognised prefixes stay inside the value and must still meet that field's rules: `z/unit` can be address text but is not a valid phone number. Local name forms `s/o` and `d/o` are ordinary name text for add/edit. Explicit search reserves `n/`, `p/` and `t/` and accepts only one field.

Prefer `add`/`edit`/`followup` to changing saved files directly. If you must edit `data/addressbook.json`, **close the app first and back up the complete file**. The [Developer Guide's saved-data description](DeveloperGuide.html#saved-client-loading) contains the schema and detailed validation rules.

- Save as **UTF-8**. A single leading byte-order mark (BOM), as added by some editors, is accepted. Invalid byte sequences or invalid saved character sequences are rejected, even when a JSON escape is syntactically valid.
- Contact fields, tags, dates and descriptions must be JSON strings. Keep phone values quoted to retain leading zeroes. IDs/counters are numbers; do not convert them to strings.

- Keep property names exact, including `persons`, `tags` and `followUp`. Unknown fields, repeated properties in one object, invalid/duplicate clients, missing required values and invalid identity metadata are rejected. When loading reports a data error, the app opens a protected empty workspace; see the [startup limitation and recovery steps](#saved-data-warning-and-recovery) for extremely deeply nested files. Optional missing tags mean no tags; absent/null `followUp` means no action. Valid overdue dates remain supported.

- A legacy file with **no identity metadata** loads valid clients with insertion-order IDs, starting at 1, without rewriting the file. The first successfully saved change writes IDs and the next-ID counter.

- Keep every `clientId` and the root `nextClientId` when copying/backing up. If any identity metadata remains, incomplete/invalid metadata is rejected. If **all** IDs and the counter are removed or set to `null`, the file is treated as legacy and receives a new ID history; discarded IDs and the old counter cannot be reconstructed. Restoring an older backup can also restore older history.

- Do not change paths or saved files externally while PolicyHarbor is running. Symbolic-link save checks do not synchronise with external filesystem changes. Repairing a file during a protected session cannot unlock it; close and restart after repair.

**Repeated properties are different from repeated fields across clients.** Two `email` properties inside one client object are rejected even if both contain the same address; one `email` property in each of two separate client objects is normal. The same rule applies to `persons` in the outer object and `description` inside a follow-up. Before removing a repeated property, compare both values with your backup so that you do not discard clients or follow-up details that need to be recovered.

- **A light dashboard for daily client work.** A branded header, command bar, numbered client table and independently scrollable profile/follow-up panels replace the previous workspace. Drag the main and sidebar dividers to allocate space.

- **All pending actions stay visible while searching.** The new unnumbered sidebar includes every client's pending action, grouped into Overdue, Due Today and Upcoming. Filtering the table does not hide other clients' upcoming work. Each card includes the full action and due date.

- **A compact client table with safe command indices.** Names and contact values wrap; pending mode adds due-date and status columns. Sorting is disabled so displayed row numbers always match `view`, `delete` and `followup`. Narrow tables scroll horizontally.

- **A clearer selected-client profile.** Contact fields, sorted tag chips and the next follow-up appear in a light card. VIEWING markers follow the selected record across follow-up reordering, including clients who share a name.
- **Run commands with Enter or Run.** Both use the same submission path. Failed commands retain their input and restore typing focus; successful commands clear it.

- **Readable success and error feedback.** A compact, read-only strip wraps and scrolls complete messages. Errors have a text label as well as color; the next successful command clears the error state. The saved-data warning remains separate and persistent.
- **Refreshed Help and data-file information.** Help offers a selectable guide link, a Copy link button and Escape-to-close. The footer exposes long data paths in a wrapped tooltip.

- **Integrated regression protection.** Tests cover the complete feed, stable pending projection, view/selection consistency, save-failure isolation, date refresh and window cleanup. Developer runs and tests enable assertions without requiring users to launch with them.

- **Safer saved-data loading.** JSON files with trailing non-whitespace content or additional root values are rejected instead of partially accepted. Invalid saved client data starts a protected session that blocks changes and preserves the original file.
- **More reliable email validation.** Iterative character scanning preserves the supported client email formats while avoiding stack overflow on unusually long inputs.
The existing seven commands and local JSON format are preserved. Each client still has one pending action; multiple actions, history, notifications and typed contact editing are outside this release.
